title: Variability arises mainly from effects on reproductive elements before conception

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Variability arises mainly from effects on reproductive elements before conception

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The most frequent cause of variability is that the male and female reproductive elements have been affected by the conditions of life before conception, the reproductive system being more sensitive to changed conditions than any other part of the organisation.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: But I am strongly inclined to suspect that the most frequent cause of variability may be attributed to the male and female reproductive elements having been affected prior to the act of conception.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter I, “Variation under Domestication”; section “Causes of Variability”. Scope: animals and plants under domestication or confinement

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch01-03: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.44

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Modern parental-exposure studies can test specific cases, but public data are fragmented and molecular proxies do not establish the most frequent cause of organismal variability. A representative coordinated dataset would be needed.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare de novo mutation, epimutation and offspring variance after documented preconception environmental exposures of both parents, against unexposed controls and effects arising after conception. Predominantly preconception-mediated variance would support the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Exposure, gamete state and offspring phenotype are rarely linked.

The proposed predominance requires representative cross-taxon data.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The mechanism can be stated in modern variables, as environmentally induced germline change versus ordinary mutation. Public archives do not contain the paired measurements that would show it is the most frequent cause, or that the reproductive system is uniquely sensitive, across animals and plants under domestication. A test would require new compilation at best and new designs for most species.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure the share of new heritable variation attributable to pre-conception environmental effects on gametes, relative to spontaneous mutation and recombination, across domesticated and confined species, and compare environmental sensitivity of reproductive failure with sensitivity of other organ systems. The reproductive-element account would be supported if that pathway explained more new variation than the alternatives and if reproduction failed under milder environmental change than other systems.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Epigenetic and mutation-rate studies cover a few model species and are not harmonized.

Zoo and studbook reproductive-failure records that might speak to sensitivity of the reproductive system are not generally public.

No open database records pre-conception environments, gamete state, and offspring heritable variance for the same individuals.

data adequacy: 0.12
discriminating power: 0.26
